questions.question: A person crosses a 900-metre long street in 6 minutes. The speed of the person, in km/h, is:

questions.question: The first shirt is sold at twice the selling price of the second shirt. The first shirt is sold at 8% profit and the second shirt is sold at a 3% loss. What is the overall percentage profit on the shirts (Rounded off to two decimal place)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First shirt sold at 8% profit

Second shirt sold at 3% loss

SP of first shirt = 2 × SP of second shirt

**Formula used:**

CP on profit = SP × 100/(100 + Profit)

CP on loss = SP × 100/(100 - Loss)

**Calculations:**

Let, SP of second shirt = 100

So, SP of first shirt = 200

CP of first shirt = 200 × 100/(100 + 8) = 20000/108 = 185.18

CP of second shirt = 100 × 100/(100 - 3) = 10000/97 = 103.09

Overall profit = (200 + 100) - (185.18 + 103.09)

⇒ 300 - 288.27 = 11.73

% profit = 11.73/(185.18 + 103.09) × 100

⇒ 11.73/288.27 × 100 = 1173/288.27 = 4.069 ≈ 4.07% 

**∴ The overall profit on the two shirts is 4.07%.**

questions.question: A man spends 72% of his salary and saves Rs. 5,740 per month. What is 10% of his annual salary (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Savings % = 100% − 72% = 28%

28% of monthly salary = Rs. 5,740

1% of monthly salary = 5,740 ÷ 28 = Rs. 205

10% of annual salary = 1.2 × monthly salary (since 10% of 12 months = 1.2 months)

Required value = 1.2 × 100 × 205 = 120 × 205 = Rs. 24,600

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Spend = 72% | Monthly Savings = Rs. 5,740

**Formula Used:**

Salary = Expenditure + Savings | Annual Salary = Monthly Salary × 12

Spend (72%)Save (28%)
28% = Rs. 5,740Monthly Salary (100%)

⇒ Monthly Savings % = 100% − 72% = 28%

⇒ 28% of Monthly Salary = 5,740

⇒ 1% of Monthly Salary = 5,740 ÷ 28 = 205

⇒ Monthly Salary = 205 × 100 = 20,500

⇒ Annual Salary = 20,500 × 12 = 2,46,000

⇒ 10% of Annual Salary = 2,46,000 × 10/100 = 24,600

**∴ The correct option is B.**

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = (Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value × 100

Salary Distribution

Income is always taken as 100%. If a person spends x% and saves y%, then x + y = 100.

Annual Conversion

Annual Salary = Monthly Salary × 12. To find p% of Annual Salary, use (p/100) × 12 × Monthly Salary.

questions.question: If a + b = 10 and ab = 6, then the value of a³ + b³ is:
questions.solution:
**Given : **

a + b = 10

ab = 6

**Formula Used : **

a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a² + b² - ab)

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculation : **

⇒ 10² = a2 + b2 + 2 × 6

⇒ a2 + b2 = 100 - 12 = 88

⇒ a3 + b3 = 10 × (88 - 6)

⇒ a3 + b3 = 10 × 82 = 820

**∴ The correct answer is 820.**

⇒ sin2θ + 1 = 2sin θ

⇒ sin θ = 1

⇒ cosec θ = 2 -1 = 1

Now, sin5θ + cosec5θ = (1)5 + (1)5 = 1 + 1 = 2

questions.question: The largest number of four digits that is exactly divisible by 17 and 36 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **LCM** of 17 and 36 first.

**LCM** (17, 36) = 17 × 36 = 612 (since 17 is a **prime number**).

Divide the largest 4-digit number (9999) by 612 to find the remainder.

9999 ÷ 612 → Remainder = 207.

**Largest number** = 9999 − 207 = 9792.

**∴ The correct answer is 9792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors are 17 and 36. We need the **largest 4-digit number**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea8b0e82bff709c86f5c696dbe4a1847f9e47e24aa2f19d36a3869ed01f8d5e9.png] 

**Step 1:** Calculate **LCM** of 17 and 36.

⇒ 17 is prime, 36 = 2² × 3².

⇒ **LCM** = 17 × 36 = 612.

**Step 2:** Find the largest 4-digit multiple of 612.

⇒ Largest 4-digit number = 9999.

⇒ 9999 ÷ 612 = 16.33...

⇒ Required number = 612 × 16.

⇒ 612 × 16 = 9792.

**∴ The correct answer is 9792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM of Prime and Composite Numbers

If one number is **prime** and doesn't divide the other, their **LCM** is simply their product.

Divisibility Rule of 36

A number is divisible by 36 if it is divisible by both 4 (last two digits) and 9 (sum of digits).

Finding Multiples near a limit

To find the largest multiple of **n** below **L**, calculate **L − (L mod n)**.</p

questions.question: If a truck moves at a constant speed of 30 km/h for 1 kilometre and 45 km/h for the next 1 kilometre. What is the average speed of the truck?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When a **truck** covers two equal distances at different speeds, the **Average Speed** is the **Harmonic Mean** of the two speeds.

Formula: Average Speed = (2 × v₁ × v₂) ÷ (v₁ + v₂)

Calculation: (2 × 30 × 45) ÷ (30 + 45) = 2700 ÷ 75 = 36 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First speed (v₁) = 30 km/h, Distance (d₁) = 1 km

Second speed (v₂) = 45 km/h, Distance (d₂) = 1 km

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf2cc828a1611862b2c39fa5b5a51d51ba8203d77e90643be407833937ecf4fc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 1 km + 1 km = 2 km

⇒ Time taken for the first km (t₁) = Distance ÷ Speed = 1/30 hours

⇒ Time taken for the second km (t₂) = Distance ÷ Speed = 1/45 hours

⇒ Total Time = t₁ + t₂ = 1/30 + 1/45

⇒ Total Time = (3 + 2) ÷ 90 = 5/90 = 1/18 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 2 ÷ (1/18) = 2 × 18

⇒ Average Speed = 36 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Average Speed

Average speed is always calculated as the **Total Distance** divided by the **Total Time** taken for the entire journey.

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a body travels for two equal time intervals at speeds x and y, the average speed is the **Arithmetic Mean**: (x + y) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: If cos θ - sin θ = √2 sin θ, then (cos θ + sin θ) is:
questions.solution:
**Given : **

cos θ - sin θ = √2 sin θ

**Calculation : **

⇒ cosθ = (√2 + 1)sinθ 

⇒ sinθ = cosθ /(√2 + 1)

Now putting value of sinθ :

⇒ cosθ + sinθ 

⇒ cosθ + cosθ/(√2 + 1)

⇒ cosθ [1 + 1/√2 + 1]

⇒ cosθ [√2 + 2/√2 + 1]

⇒ cosθ [√2 + 2 × √2 - 1/2 -1]

⇒ cosθ [2 - √2 + 2√2 - 2/1]

⇒ √2 cosθ 

**∴ The correct answer is √2 cosθ.**

questions.question: Let the speed of the boat in still water be 17 km/h and let the speed of the stream be 5 km/h. What is the time taken by the boat to go 110 km downstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream = 17 + 5 = 22 km/h.

Time = Distance ÷ Downstream speed = 110 ÷ 22 = 5 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water = 17 km/h

Speed of stream = 5 km/h

Distance to travel downstream = 110 km

**Formula Used:**

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2103eedb8205a8f51ef5c551e767c949f21f015ec296db194dcfb5f7c5247974.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Downstream speed = 17 + 5 = 22 km/h

⇒ Time taken = Distance ÷ Downstream speed

⇒ Time taken = 110 ÷ 22

⇒ Time taken = 5 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Upstream Speed

Upstream speed is the relative speed of the boat when traveling against the flow of the river. Formula: Upstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water − Speed of stream.

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If both downstream and upstream speeds are given, you can calculate the boat's speed as: Speed of boat = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

Similarly, the speed of the current can be found using: Speed of stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.
